title: Levels in a Zigzag

concept.title: Take the levels as usual, and reverse every second one
body: In a zigzag walk the first level is read from left to right, the second from right to left, the third from left to right again, and so on. The simplest way: get each level with the ordinary level-order walk and **reverse every second level** (the levels with an odd index, counting from 0).

body.code:
rows = []
level = [root]
left_to_right = True
while level:
    values = [node.val for node in level]
    rows.append(values if left_to_right else values[::-1])
    left_to_right = not left_to_right
    level = [child for node in level for child in (node.left, node.right) if child is not None]

body: The order in which the **next** level is built does not change: it is always from left to right. Only the way the values are written down alternates. Keep these two things apart: the traversal order and the output order.

statement: Print the values of a binary tree level by level, in a zigzag: the first level from left to right, the second level from right to left, the third level from left to right, and so on. Every level is one line.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.
hints: Get the levels one by one as in the ordinary level-order walk.
Reverse every second level when you write it.
Building the next level always goes from left to right.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root

    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def zigzag(root):
    rows = []
    level = [root]
    forward = True
    while level:
        values = [node.val for node in level]
        rows.append(values if forward else values[::-1])
        forward = not forward
        level = [child for node in level for child in (node.left, node.right) if child is not None]
    return rows

t = int(input())
vals = input().split()

for row in zigzag(build_tree(vals)):
    print(*row)
